0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 2 ) ( Third Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 June 1983, after the draft finalized by the Doon, Windows and Shutters Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council.

0.2 This standard was fint 'published in 1962 and subsequently revised
in 1966 and 1980. During this period the standard hal undergone modifications relating to grade of doors, species of timber, etc, and the lizes were rationaJi.d.
O.S Keeping in view the advantagls of modular co-ordination. Indian Standarda lpeciCy the dimensioDs of components in modular units. In 'line with this, the dimensiolll of ahutters were also specified in modular units. However, it was repeatedly brought to the notice the Committee. that there wu sufficient demand for lizes other than modular lizes and that the manufacturers were meeting Iuch demands at present. Thi. had led to a situation where Ihutten iatisfyiog the other requirements of the standard, but not the requirements reg~rding the dimenlions were

or

el. .iied as Dot satisfyiDI the requiremenu.:()f the standard. This lituation allO came in the way of satisfying the CODs~mer needs Cor other quality requirements by a third party inspection I,.tem. Therefore, with � view to encouraging productioD of timber .butten to the quality nquiremeatl lpecified in the .tandard, the Committee reviewed the relevant clausea 'of the Indian Standard, and decided to relax the dimenlional requirementl in this third revi.ion by permittiDR non-modular Iiselln .aditioD to the modular aizes lpeci6ed in the standard at preseut. However. the relaxation haa been made only in the height and width, the thicbe.. remaining uDchanpd from the present provilloDie This

3

18 I 2111 ( Part 2 ) � 1983 relaxation will be for a period of four years from the publication of this standard and it is intended that the manufacturers and consumers organizations can gradually switch over within this period to the modular sizes, which are the preferred sizes.

0.3.1 Wooden flush door Ihutten using particle board for face panel.
are generally manufactured in the same way as the doors with plywood

face panels. This standard, therefore, covers only the nec.&ry requirements and provisions which are additional or alternative to those covered in IS : 2191 ( Part� 1 )�1983~.
0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value. observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-1960f. The number of significant places retained in the rounded ofF value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard (Part 2) lay. down the requirements regarding material, grade, types, sizes, construction, finishes and tests of wooden flush door shutten of cellular and hollow core type with particle board race panels (both veneered and unveneered ] and hard-board face

panels.
2. TYPES AND DESIGNATION
2.1 Cellular and hollow solid core flush door shutters with particle board face panels may be of the decorative type or non-decorative ( paintable ) type. The designation of various types of .hutters shall be bued on the type of core and the type of face panel as given in Table 1.

3. SIZES AND TOLERANCES
3.1 Sizes of the door shutters shall generally conform to the modular

sizes specified in Table 2 (I" allD Fig. 1). Sizes other than modular sizes, as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser, may allo be permitted; however, the thickness of shutters in such cue. shall not be less than those specified against the nearest higher modular size given in 3.2.
